pages.title: Complex Plane
pages.text: The real line, with the imaginary unit laid at right angles across it, forming a flat sheet of numbers. On this plane every polynomial has all its roots, multiplication is rotation and scaling, and smooth functions become astonishingly rigid. It feels like a perfectly flat, perfectly thin pane of glass.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)With i in hand, the obvious step was to cross it with the real continuum. The Analytic Continuator held the two at right angles in a condensate until they fused into one field of numbers, two dimensions wide.
